summary.intent: Plan and then execute Phase 69 (FUSE and WinFsp Rust integration with grant-root awareness) end-to-end via the GSD workflow — research, plan, verify, then auto-advance into wave-based parallel execution — for the cipher-box-phase69 worktree.
summary.outcome: Planning completed: research/validation/patterns committed, 14 plans across 7 waves written (recovering from a mid-session planner crash by resuming with a single-plan planner for the missing 69-14), plan-checker passed, requirements/decision coverage gates passed, and everything committed (`23b4ba198`). Execution then began with worktree-isolated wave-based parallelism; a synchronous canary (69-01) validated the executor→worktree→merge→cargo pipeline, and Wave 1 (69-01/69-02/69-03, 3 of 14 plans) completed with all cargo checks and tests green, with Wave 2 setup underway when the transcript ends.

repo: gsd-tools commit helper has a known false-negative: it reports `commit_failed` even when the commit and lint-staged actually succeeded — always verify via `git log` before retrying.

API-SURFACE regen (intel plan:pre hook) returns `symbolCount: 0, stale: true` for Rust-only phases since the extractor is TS/JS-focused; safe to omit from planner prompts when RESEARCH.md already has verified symbol locations.

Non-blocking drift-gate findings can be dominated by noise outside the phase's actual crates (`.claude/`, `.learnings/`, `landing/`, root config) — check file paths before treating action_required as meaningful.
Worktree agents spawned without `node_modules` fail their first commit attempt via husky/lint-staged (`lint-staged not found`) until `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is run inside the worktree.
`cipher-box-phase69` is itself a linked git worktree of the `cipher-box` repo — nested worktree-of-worktree orchestration, so manifest `orchestrator_root` pinning matters for correct merge-back.

The desktop E2E GitHub Actions workflow's real name is "Desktop E2E Tests", not "CI E2E Tests" as ROADMAP.md/CONTEXT.md word it — using the wrong name in `gh workflow run` would 404 (relates to [[project-cipherbox-desktop-e2e-mjs]]).

`SentShareResponseDto` (apps/api/src/shares/dto/share-response.dto.ts) has no `revoked`/status field because shares are hard-deleted on revoke — every row returned by `GET /shares/sent` is inherently an active grant.
`crates/api-client` had no wrapper for `GET /shares/sent` prior to this phase; `activeGrantRootIpnsNames` depends on it — a hidden blast-radius item surfaced by the phase researcher.

code.finding: Complete TS reference implementation for the grant-root scope algorithm — the Rust port (crates/fuse/src/write_ops/) is a port, not a design-from-scratch, per phase 69 research.

TS source ported into crates/sdk/src/rotation/high_water.rs (RotationHighWater<S: HighWaterStore>, fail-closed enforce_resolved) plus a new JsonSidecarFloorStore durable implementation with no new storage dependency.
Flagged by the pattern-mapper as thin-precedent (weak existing Rust analog) alongside write_ops/grant_scope.rs.

workflow: Filesystem-fallback recovery: when a planner subagent dies mid-response (API connection error), inspect what was actually written to disk (frontmatter validity, close tags, requirement coverage) before deciding to resume vs. restart — resumed here by spawning a fresh single-plan-mode planner for just the missing plan rather than restarting the whole batch.

Canary-first parallel dispatch: run the first plan of a wave synchronously end-to-end (executor → worktree → merge → post-merge build gate) to validate the pipeline before fanning out the rest of the wave in parallel background agents.

Requirements-ID drift risk: a planner used internal pseudo-IDs (SC-01..SC-06) in plan frontmatter instead of the actual phase requirement ID (TEST-03); the §13 requirements-coverage gate is what catches this class of mismatch, not manual review alone.
Durable handoff files written to a scratchpad path before a scheduled pause (ScheduleWakeup) protect against context summarization losing recovery state across a long wall-clock gap.
Role separation preserved during recovery: orchestrator did not author the missing plan inline, instead spawned a fresh gsd-planner agent even for single-plan recovery mode.

friction: gsd-planner subagent hit an API error (connection closed mid-response) and crashed after writing only 13 of 14 required plans, requiring a recovery/pause/resume cycle.

Commit helper reported `commit_failed` twice (once for VALIDATION.md, once for the final 14-plan commit) despite the commits actually landing — a recurring false-negative that requires manual git log verification each time.
API-SURFACE regeneration hook is a no-op/stale for Rust phases, adding a step that yields nothing useful.
STATE.md and ROADMAP annotate calls in §13b/§13c turned out to be idempotent no-ops, requiring extra verification to confirm nothing was missed.
Worktree agent for 69-02 hit a husky pre-commit failure on first commit due to missing node_modules, requiring an ad hoc pnpm install inside the worktree.
